skill.name: plan-my-week
skill.description: Plan a week or a month of Twitter or LinkedIn posts as a dated calendar, with a topic, format, opening line and purpose for each one. Use when someone asks for a content plan, a posting schedule, a content calendar, a week of posts, or help posting consistently. Do not use it to write one post, and do not schedule or publish anything without the person seeing it first.
skill.summary: Create a practical Twitter or LinkedIn content calendar with topics, formats, hooks, purposes, and approval-aware scheduling.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.user_title: Plan a Week of Social Posts
content.value_statement: Consistent social posting is difficult when topics, formats, and opening lines remain undecided. This skill creates a dated Twitter or LinkedIn calendar with varied formats, clear purposes, and optional per-post scheduling approval.
actual_capabilities: Clarifies the platform, posting frequency, content pillars, and time zone before planning.
Creates a dated table with a pillar, format, working title, opening line, and purpose for each post.
Rotates pillars and formats, limits repeated calls to action, and leaves one flexible slot.
Provides the plan as a table and as plain text for reuse in another tool.
Uses VoiceMOAT profiles, ideas, hooks, and one-post approval scheduling when the account is connected.
limitations: It plans Twitter and LinkedIn content rather than content for other platforms.
It does not write full posts unless the user asks for drafting.
It does not claim an optimal posting time without the user's analytics.
VoiceMOAT scheduling requires a connected Pro or Enterprise account and approval for each post.

use_cases.title: Build a Founder Content Routine
use_cases.description: Turn three or four recurring expertise areas into a manageable weekly calendar with varied formats and ready-to-use opening lines.

use_cases.title: Plan a LinkedIn Thought Leadership Week
use_cases.description: Organize professional topics across a week while keeping each post focused, purposeful, and aligned with the author's available time.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Approved Publishing Queue
use_cases.description: Use a connected VoiceMOAT account to develop ideas and review each exact post before placing approved posts in the publishing queue.
use_cases.target_user: Content managers and small marketing teams

prompt_templates.title: Create My First Weekly Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a one-week content calendar for LinkedIn with three posts. Use these pillars: [pillars]. Ask any missing planning questions first.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning with a small, repeatable schedule

prompt_templates.title: Plan Around My Content Pillars
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a seven-post Twitter calendar from these pillars: [pillars]. Rotate the pillars, vary the formats, include an opening line and purpose, and leave one flexible slot.
prompt_templates.scenario: A regular poster needs structure and variety

prompt_templates.title: Balance Two Platform Plans
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between Twitter and LinkedIn, then create a monthly plan for [number] posts. Use my time zone, audience information, pillars, and preferred formats.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced creator needs a longer schedule

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a VoiceMOAT Queue
prompt_templates.prompt: Using my connected VoiceMOAT account, create a weekly plan from my voice profile and content pillars. Show the exact text, account, and time for each post, and request approval before scheduling each one.

output_examples.input: Create a three-post LinkedIn plan for a product consultant. Use product discovery, customer research, and team leadership as pillars.
output_examples.output:
Date | Pillar | Format | Working title | Opening line | Purpose
Monday | Product discovery | Short lesson | The interview question I stopped asking | Most discovery calls fail before the first answer. | Teach a practical method
Wednesday | Customer research | Story | What one customer changed | A single customer comment changed our roadmap. | Show evidence-based learning
Friday | Team leadership | Checklist | A calmer research handoff | A clear handoff prevents three avoidable meetings. | Offer a useful process

output_examples.input: Plan five Twitter posts for a solo founder with a flexible slot.
output: Monday: Founder lesson, short thread, opening line: The fastest way to learn is to ship a smaller test.
Tuesday: Customer insight, question, opening line: What do users explain better than your dashboard?
Thursday: Process note, checklist, opening line: Three decisions make a weekly review useful.
Friday: Personal observation, short post, opening line: A slower week revealed the work worth keeping.
Flexible slot: Leave open for a timely lesson or event.

best_practices: Provide the platform, number of posts, pillars, time zone, and audience context.
Use analytics when available, and label any suggested posting time as adjustable.
Review the exact text, account, and time before approving each scheduled post.
anti_patterns: Do not request a large schedule before establishing a sustainable posting habit.
Do not repeat one pillar, format, or call to action throughout the whole plan.
Do not approve or publish posts without reviewing their final text and timing.

faq.question: Which platforms does this skill support?
faq.answer: It plans content for Twitter and LinkedIn.

faq.question: Does it write the posts for me?
faq.answer: It provides topics, formats, opening lines, and purposes. Ask separately when you want full drafts.

faq.question: How many posts should I plan?
faq.answer: Choose a number that fits your real routine. A smaller weekly plan is easier to maintain.

faq.question: Can it choose the best posting time?
faq.answer: It uses your analytics when available. Otherwise, it suggests a reasonable time that you can change.

faq.question: Can it schedule posts automatically?
faq.answer: A connected VoiceMOAT account can place approved posts in its publishing queue. Each post requires separate approval.

faq.question: What does the flexible slot do?
faq.answer: It leaves room for a timely event, lesson, or idea that appears during the week.
